title: Types of employment
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches this brief: ecb-types-work covers full-time, part-time, casual and unpaid work but not contractors or casual loading, and ecb-casual-gig-work covers casual loading and gig work but not full-time, part-time or contractors, so no single point fits without adding a new idea.

draft.title: Types of employment
card: these workers have regular hours each week and get paid leave, such as annual leave and sick leave. Full-time workers work more hours than part-time workers.
these workers have no guaranteed hours and no paid leave. They usually get a higher hourly rate to make up for this.
a person who works for themselves and is paid for each job or project, rather than being an employee of one business.
Each type has trade-offs. Regular hours and paid leave give more certainty. A higher hourly rate comes with less certainty about how much work there will be.
draft.remember: Regular hours and paid leave, or a higher hourly rate with no guarantees, or working for yourself.

a.q: Jai works at a pool. His hours change each week, he gets no paid sick leave, and his hourly rate is higher than other staff. What type of worker is he?
a.why: Hours that are not guaranteed, no paid leave and a higher hourly rate are the signs of casual work. A part-time worker also works fewer hours, but has regular hours and paid leave.
a.clue: Which type has no guaranteed hours?

b.q: Priya is a part-time worker at a bakery in Bendigo. Her friend Sam works casual shifts at a nearby café. Which statement about them is correct?
opts: Priya has paid leave, but Sam does not
Sam has paid leave, but Priya does not
Priya has a higher hourly rate than Sam
Sam has more certain hours than Priya
b.why: Part-time workers get paid leave, while casual workers do not. Casual workers usually have a higher hourly rate to make up for it, so Priya's rate is not likely to be higher.
b.clue: Which of the two has regular hours and paid leave?

b.best: Priya has paid leave, but Sam does not
